subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: The cramped commercial-towing-crew galley of a 1979 retro-futurist starfreighter: gridded deck, cream panel walls with dark seams, a counter run with coffee maker and CRT, a central mess table and overhead ductwork.
spec.layout: A single room module, +Z is the open end where crew enters, -Z the aft wall. Standing on y = 0 is the deck: full-width plating, checker plate, open grating strips and yellow-black hazard stripes at the entry. Against the aft wall (-Z) runs the work counter: lower cabinets, a worktop with a coffee maker, a food heater, a sink basin, and above it upper lockers, a cathode monitor on an articulated arm, pipes and conduits. Left and right walls (x = ±1.2) carry ribbed cream panels with dark seam lines, a vent grille, a switch panel with chunky toggles, a wall lamp and a small shelf with mugs. Centred on the deck sits the mess table with stools, trays, cups and a cutlery caddy, leaving ~0.5 m walkway on each side. Overhead, a ceiling soffit spans wall to wall at y = 2.05 with a recessed light tray, fat ribbed ducts running fore-aft and cable bundles dropping to the walls. The style on every part: chunky beige-cream panels inset in dark trim, exposed fasteners and greebles, matte industrial greens and greys for machines, amber indicator lamps, one green-glowing CRT, hazard yellow where feet meet equipment — flat colours, no gradients, everything boxy and riveted.

parts.builds: The galley floor of the Nostromo: a full-width base slab in deckPlate from x = -1.2 to 1.2 and z = -2.4 to 2.4, its top face at y = 0.12 (mount deckTop). On top sit raised checker-plate panels in deckChecker with visible bolt heads around each panel edge, and two open grating strips (dark recessed slots with cross ribs) running fore-aft along the walkways at x = ±0.65. At the entry end (z = +2.2 to 2.4) lay a yellow-black hazard stripe strip in hazard and trimDark. Add floor greebles: a low cable conduit box in trimDark running along one wall base with a rubber cable in rubber lying beside it, a circular deck drain in steel, a small hatch plate with a folding handle, and a scuffed dark patch near the table where boots land (a shadowInk flat decal plate). Keep everything flush or nearly flush — nothing stands higher than 0.06 above deckTop.
parts.attaches: Owns y = 0. Its top face is mount deckTop; walls, table and stools all start at deckTop.

parts.builds: The aft wall (-Z) and its full work-counter run, the galley's hero piece. The wall itself is chunky cream panels (panelCream) inset in a grid of trimDark seam frames with rivet studs, facing +Z at z = -2.4 (mount aftWallFace at its mid-line). In front of it, from z = -2.4 forward to z = -1.7: lower cabinets in machineGreen with trimDark kick plates, chunky handles and a yellow hazard stripe along the toe line; a steel worktop at y = 0.95. On the worktop, left to right: a coffee maker — a boxy machineGreen body with a steel spout, a glass pot (utensil, slightly translucent-looking pale fill), amber indicator lamp and a cup resting on its drip tray; a food heater — a riveted steel box with a dark door window, red warning lamp and hazard-edged door handle; a sink basin in steel with a pipe faucet and a stack of two tin trays. Above the worktop: a row of upper lockers in panelCream with trimDark latches, then a CRT monitor in a greebleGrey housing on a jointed steel arm, its screen a glowing crtGlow green rectangle set in trimDark bezel with a small amber power lamp; a backboard of conduit in trimDark carrying copper pipes and a red valve wheel; a paper printout pinned up (a small white panel with trimDark marks). Every lamp is a small separate glowing part: amber for status, warningRed for the heater.
parts.attaches: Sits on mount deckTop (cabinet bases at y = 0.12), wall back plane at z = -2.4 meets the deck's aft edge; side edges at x = ±1.2 meet the side walls' aft ends.

parts.builds: Both side walls of the galley, mirrored left and right, each a plane of ribbed cream panels at x = ±1.2 with frames of trimDark seams, rivets and one big recessed access panel per wall. Built as one part: build the left wall, then mirror. Each wall carries, fore to aft: a wall lamp — a steel hood with an amber-tinted underside lens; a ribbed vent grille in greebleGrey with trimDark frame; a switch panel in panelCream holding six chunky toggle switches (steel levers, trimDark bases) with one amberLamp and one warningRed indicator beside them; a small steel shelf near the aft end holding three mismatched mugs (greebleGrey, machineGreen, copper) and a spoon caddy; and low down, a floor-level cable clamp plate in trimDark with two rubber cable loops entering the wall. The right wall swaps the shelf for a wall-mounted fire extinguisher (warningRed body, steel nozzle, hazard band). Panels use panelCream with the lit variant panelCreamLit on surfaces angled toward the ceiling light tray. Wall plane at x = ±1.0 toward the interior (mounts sideWallFaceL / sideWallFaceR) so deck conduit and table clear it.
parts.attaches: Bases sit on mount deckTop at y = 0.12; interior wall planes are the mounts sideWallFaceL and sideWallFaceR where the ceiling soffit ends and counter run abuts; aft ends butt against the aft wall at z = -2.4.

parts.builds: The central mess table and stools, the room's social heart, echoing the iconic crew-table scene. A heavy cylindrical pedestal base in trimDark standing on mount deckTop, a chunky fluted column in hull grey, and a round table top in tableTop at y = 0.78 with a steel rim ring and bolt heads around its edge. On the tabletop, arranged mid-meal: two steel food trays (greebleGrey) with inset compartments — one holding a wedge of dark food and a pale blob, the other empty; two mugs (one machineGreen, one utensil white) with tiny amber steam wisps as thin standing spikes; a cutlery caddy (trimDark) with steel utensil handles sticking out; a small stack of paper printouts in white with trimDark line marks; and a dented cup knocked on its side. Around the table, three stools: each a trimDark base on deckTop, a thick cylinder seat in hull with a panelCream cushion pad, and a slight height stagger. One stool is pushed back and turned a little, as if someone just left. Add a low profile — the whole part stays under y = 1.0 so sightlines to the counter stay open.
parts.attaches: Stands alone on mount deckTop, centred near [0, 0.12, 0.05]; clear of the counter front (z = -1.7) by ~0.8 m and of both walls by ~0.35 m.

parts.builds: The overhead: a soffit slab in hull spanning wall to wall from x = -1.2 to 1.2 and z = -2.4 to 2.4, its underside at y = 2.05 (mount ceilingSoffit), boxed in trimDark perimeter frame. Recessed into its underside, centred, a long rectangular light tray: a trimDark frame, a bright panelCreamLit diffuser and a steel grille over it — the galley's main light. Running fore-aft alongside it, two fat ribbed ducts in greebleGrey with steel ring ribs every 0.25 m and a slight sag of character; they hang to y = 1.95, low enough to feel oppressive. Where ducts meet the aft wall, a square plenum box in machineGreen with copper pipe stubs and a red valve. Along one side, a bundle of rubber cables in rubber clamped in steel saddles, dropping from soffit to the switch-panel area of the side walls. Add greebles: a hanging chain hook (steel links) from the soffit above the table, an amber rotating-beacon dome (amberLamp, glowing) near the entry end, and a small speaker grille in trimDark. Everything above y = 1.9 except the beacon and hook.
parts.attaches: Its edge beams land on the side walls' tops at the mounts sideWallFaceL / sideWallFaceR and on the aft wall top at aftWallFace; soffit underside at ceilingSoffit, y = 2.05.
